title: Army Jawan Arrested for Strangling Pregnant Wife, Tried to Pass Off Death as Accidental Fall
excerpt: Dnyaneshwar Madne of the 6 Maratha Battalion allegedly killed his seven-month-pregnant wife Dipali in Washim, Maharashtra; doctors spotted neck injuries and alerted police.
body:
• Dnyaneshwar Madne, 28, a jawan with the Army's 6 Maratha Battalion, was arrested in Washim, Maharashtra for allegedly strangling his seven-month-pregnant wife Dipali.
  • Madne tried to present the death as an accidental fall; doctors at a government hospital noticed neck injuries and alerted police.
  • The victim's family alleges Madne was involved in an extramarital affair and had been harassing Dipali for months.
  • Murder charges have been filed against Madne and his parents.

A 28-year-old Indian Army jawan has been arrested in Maharashtra's Washim district for allegedly strangling his seven-month-pregnant wife and attempting to pass off her death as an accidental fall, police said.

How the Crime Unravelled

The accused, Dnyaneshwar Madne, serves with the Army's 6 Maratha Battalion. On August 6, he called his wife Dipali's family in Burhanpur, Madhya Pradesh, around 3 pm and told them she had fallen at home while doing household work and been admitted to hospital.

Dipali's brother, Rahul Mane, said the family left immediately and reached Washim around 7 pm. By then, Dipali had been moved from a private hospital — where Madne had arranged an ambulance — to a government facility.

At the government hospital, doctors noticed clear injury marks on the woman's neck that were inconsistent with a fall. They informed police.

"When our team reached the hospital, it was apparent that something was wrong. There were visible injury marks on the woman's neck."

— Manish Thakre, Senior Police Officer, Washim

Investigators believe an argument between the couple escalated at their residence, during which Madne allegedly strangled Dipali. Police noted that the accused was scheduled to leave for duty in Jammu and Kashmir the following day.

Family Alleges Harassment and Affair

Rahul Mane has alleged that Madne was involved in an extramarital relationship and had been harassing Dipali over the issue for a prolonged period. The family claims tensions had escalated months earlier, prompting both sides to hold a meeting to resolve the dispute. While the matter appeared settled at the time, the family says the harassment continued.

These allegations form part of the formal complaint that led to murder charges.

Police Action

Washim police arrested Madne and registered a murder case against him and his parents. The parents' precise role, if any, remains under investigation. The medical findings — neck injuries inconsistent with a fall — form the core of the prosecution's case. Further forensic examination and witness statements are expected to establish the full sequence of events.

The case is among several recent incidents involving serving soldiers accused of domestic violence. All allegations remain subject to judicial scrutiny, and the accused is entitled to due process.
